spec.description: vLLM Inference Server Monitoring

spec.title: Success Rate
spec.description: Request success rate. Normal (green) if 99.5% or above, risky (red) if below 98%. Only counts successful completions where finished_reason='stop'.

spec.title: Active Requests
spec.description: Number of currently processing (Running) + waiting (Waiting) requests. A sudden increase is a sign of a traffic spike.

spec.title: System Efficiency
spec.description: Scheduler efficiency. Running/(Running+Waiting). 100% means all requests are processed immediately. Below 70% indicates overload.

spec.title: TTFT P99
spec.description: Time taken until the first token is generated (P99). Key metric for perceived user response speed. Ideally under 1 second.

spec.title: Preemption Rate
spec.description: [Critical] Preemption rate. Occurs when running requests are interrupted due to insufficient KV Cache. If > 0, immediate investigation is required. Consider increasing GPU memory or decreasing batch size.

spec.title: E2E Request Latency
spec.description: Total time from request receipt to response completion. P50 is the median, P99 is the 99th percentile. Spikes in P99 indicate bottlenecks.

spec.title: Inference Stage Breakdown
spec.description: Ratio of Prefill (input processing) vs Decode (output generation) latency. High prefill indicates long input prompts; high decode indicates long output generation.

spec.title: TTFT vs TPOT
spec.description: Comparison of TTFT (Time to First Token) vs TPOT (Time Per Output Token). High TTFT suggests prefill bottleneck; high TPOT suggests decode bottleneck.

spec.title: Token Throughput
spec.description: Tokens processed per second. Input(Prompt) = input tokens, Output(Generation) = output tokens. Higher throughput indicates better system efficiency.

spec.title: Token I/O Ratio
spec.description: Ratio of output tokens to input tokens. High ratio = long input + short output (RAG); low ratio = short input + long output (generation/summarization).

spec.title: Prefix Cache Savings
spec.description: Percentage of computations saved by Prefix Cache. Higher means more prefill operations are skipped via cache, saving GPU resources. (1 - actual_computed / total_input) * 100

spec.title: Request Length Heatmap (Prompt)
spec.description: Distribution of input token counts per request. Darker colors indicate more requests of that length. Concentration in certain ranges may require length-based optimization.

spec.title: Request Queue Time
spec.description: Time requests spend waiting in the queue. Increases if the GPU is busy. Persistent high values suggest a need for instance scaling.

spec.title: GPU KV Cache Usage
spec.description: GPU KV Cache usage. Memory area used to store intermediate computation results. Above 80% is caution; above 95% risks Preemption.

spec.title: Prefix Cache Hit Rate
spec.description: Prefix Cache hit rate. Percentage of requests reusing system prompts or few-shot examples. >70% is efficient; key metric for RAG environments.

spec.title: Scheduler State
spec.description: Number of requests by scheduler state. Running=inferring on GPU, Waiting=in queue, Swapped=memory swapped. Persistent increase in Waiting indicates overload.

spec.title: Python GC & Memory
spec.description: Python GC event frequency and process memory usage. Frequent GC or steadily increasing RSS may indicate a memory leak.

spec.title: Finish Reason Distribution
spec.description: Distribution of request completion reasons. stop=normal completion (EOS), length=max length reached, abort=interrupted. High abort rate is problematic.

spec.title: Throughput vs Success
spec.description: Trend of total throughput vs successful requests. A gap indicates failed requests. They should consistently match for normal operation.

spec.title: Routing Split
spec.description: Total number of requests split by classification. Shows the distribution between DIRECT and REASONING modes.

spec.title: Request Rate by Mode
spec.description: Rate of requests per second categorized by classification (DIRECT or REASONING).

spec.title: Classify Latency
spec.description: Latency of the classification process, shown in percentiles (p50, p95, p99).

spec.title: Speculative Token Acceptance Rate
spec.description: Fraction of draft tokens accepted by the main model. Higher is better. ~0.65 is good for 6 spec tokens; below 0.4 may indicate spec decode is not worth the overhead.

spec.title: Per-Position Acceptance Rate
spec.description: Acceptance rate at each draft position. Position 0 should be highest (~80%+); positions 5+ typically lowest. The curve shape helps diagnose if the draft model is too different from the main model.

spec.title: Draft vs Accepted vs Rejected Throughput
spec.description: Rate of draft tokens generated, accepted, and rejected. Rejected tokens are wasted compute (full forward pass then discard). Low acceptance relative to drafts indicates the draft model may be a poor match.

spec.title: Average Accepted Tokens per Step
spec.description: Total accepted tokens divided by position-0 acceptance rate gives the average number of tokens accepted per spec step. If this is near 1.0, most steps accept only the first token. Above 2.0 indicates strong spec decode performance.
